rules.clause: Here is the general equation for the activation (A) of a chunk i:
rules.used_as: A_i = B_i + S_i + noise (no partial matching)

rules.clause: n: The number of presentations for chunk i. tj: The time since the jth presentation.
rules.used_as: B_i = ln(sum over presentations j of t_j^-d) + beta_i

rules.clause: The recommended value for :bll is .5, and it is one of the few parameters which have a strong recommended value.

If the chunk being added is equivalent to a chunk which is already in DM, then the new chunk is merged with the existing chunk using the merge-chunks command and that chunk is strengthened by giving it another reference at the time of the merging.
rules.used_as: adding an equivalent chunk gives it another presentation

rules.clause: among the chunks which match the request the one with the highest activation value, above a parameterized threshold, is the one that will be retrieved. If no matching chunk has an activation above the threshold then a failure to retrieve occurs.
rules.used_as: the highest-activation match above the threshold is retrieved, else a failure

rules.clause: The retrieval threshold. This is the minimum activation a chunk must have to be able to be retrieved
Wkj: This is the amount of activation from source j in buffer k. It is the source activation of buffer k divided by the number of sources j in that buffer by default.
slotsj: the number of slots in which j is the value across all chunks in DM. slotsofji: the number of slots in chunk i which have j as the value (plus 1 when chunk i is chunk j).
rules.used_as: S_ji = S - ln(fan_ji), fan_ji = (1 + slots_j) / slotsof_ji

rules.clause: By default the declarative module will print a warning if S ji becomes negative due to that calculation and use 0.0 instead of the negative value
Thus they are generated from a logistic distribution with a mean of 0 and an s as specified by the corresponding parameter of the declarative module.
rules.used_as: noise = s ln(p / (1 - p)), p uniform on (0, 1)

rules.clause: RT: The time to retrieve the chunk in seconds Ai: The activation of the chunk i which is being retrieved F: The latency factor parameter f : The latency exponent parameter

If there is no chunk found in response to a request or the chunk with the highest activation is below the retrieval threshold then the time required to indicate a failure to retrieve any chunk is determined by this equation when subsymbolic computations are enabled:
rules.used_as: RT = F e^(-f tau) for a failure

rules.clause: The latency factor value, F, in the equation for retrieval times. It can be set to any non-negative value and defaults to 1.0.

The default action time parameter specifies the default time that it takes to fire a production in seconds. That is the amount of time that passes between a production’s selection and fired events. The default value is .05 (50ms)
The effective reward for a production i is the reward value received after its nth usage minus the time since that nth selection of production i.
rules.used_as: U_i(n) = U_i(n-1) + alpha (R_i(n) - U_i(n-1)), R_i(n) = reward - time since the nth selection

rules.clause: parameter in the utility learning equation. The default value is .2.

rules.used_as: the goal buffer's source activation W defaults to 0.0

rules.clause: The fan effect is the empirically observed ﬁnding that the greater the number of facts related to some concept that a subject has to memorize, the slower the subject will be to recall any one of them.
rules.used_as: the fan effect the spreading term reproduces
